subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a machine-readable Skill Workshop lifecycle contract in core, and if so should it be OpenClaw-native, AISP/AISOP, or external to ClawHub/plugin packaging?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing contract authority for Skill Workshop write, scan, approval, rollback, and target-boundary behavior is a product/security decision rather than a safe autonomous repair.

options.title: OpenClaw-native docs/tests contract
options.body: Add a narrow OpenClaw-owned contract fixture or generated test reference for the existing lifecycle invariants, with no AISP runtime dependency.

options.title: External AISP/ClawHub reference
options.body: Keep the AISP/AISOP artifact outside core as a reference package while OpenClaw core continues to own runtime enforcement and tests.

options.title: Full AISP package in core
options.body: Adopt the proposed AISP/AISOP package directly in the repository, accepting the extra review burden around authority and drift.

recommendation.title: OpenClaw-native docs/tests contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow OpenClaw-owned contract fixture or generated test reference for the existing lifecycle invariants, with no AISP runtime dependency.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history on the central Skill Workshop service, store, scanner, and rollback behavior that the contract would describe.
